gene.name: serine and arginine rich splicing factor 5
gene.function: Plays a role in constitutive splicing and can modulate the selection of alternative splice sites.

gene.name: signal transducer and activator of transcription 1
gene.function: Signal transducer and transcription activator that mediates cellular responses to interferons (IFNs), cytokine KITLG/SCF and other cytokines and other growth factors. Following type I IFN (IFN-alpha and IFN-beta) binding to cell surface receptors, signaling via protein kinases leads to activation of Jak kinases (TYK2 and JAK1) and to tyrosine phosphorylation of STAT1 and STAT2. The phosphorylated STATs dimerize and associate with ISGF3G/IRF-9 to form a complex termed ISGF3 transcription factor, that enters the nucleus. ISGF3 binds to the IFN stimulated response element (ISRE) to activate the transcription of IFN-stimulated genes (ISG), which drive the cell in an antiviral state. In response to type II IFN (IFN-gamma), STAT1 is tyrosine- and serine-phosphorylated. It then forms a homodimer termed IFN-gamma-activated factor (GAF), migrates into the nucleus and binds to the IFN gamma activated sequence (GAS) to drive the expression of the target genes, inducing a cellular antiviral state. Becomes activated in response to KITLG/SCF and KIT signaling. May mediate cellular responses to activated FGFR1, FGFR2, FGFR3 and FGFR4. Following bacterial lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced TLR4 endocytosis, phosphorylated at Thr-749 by IKBKB which promotes binding of STAT1 to the 5'-TTTGAGGC-3' sequence in the ARID5A promoter, resulting in transcriptional activation of ARID5A and subsequent ARID5A-mediated stabilization of IL6. Phosphorylation at Thr-749 also promotes binding of STAT1 to the 5'-TTTGAGTC-3' sequence in the IL12B promoter and activation of IL12B transcription. Involved in food tolerance in small intestine: associates with the Gasdermin-D, p13 cleavage product (13 kDa GSDMD) and promotes transcription of CIITA, inducing type 1 regulatory T (Tr1) cells in upper small intestine (By similarity).

gene.name: Sad1 and UNC84 domain containing 2
gene.function: As a component of the LINC (LInker of Nucleoskeleton and Cytoskeleton) complex, involved in the connection between the nuclear lamina and the cytoskeleton. The nucleocytoplasmic interactions established by the LINC complex play an important role in the transmission of mechanical forces across the nuclear envelope and in nuclear movement and positioning. Specifically, SYNE2 and SUN2 assemble in arrays of transmembrane actin-associated nuclear (TAN) lines which are bound to F-actin cables and couple the nucleus to retrograde actin flow during actin-dependent nuclear movement. Required for interkinetic nuclear migration (INM) and essential for nucleokinesis and centrosome- nucleus coupling during radial neuronal migration in the cerebral cortex and during glial migration. Required for nuclear migration in retinal photoreceptor progenitors implicating association with cytoplasmic dynein-dynactin and kinesin motor complexes, and probably B-type lamins; SUN1 and SUN2 seem to act redundantly. The SUN1/2:KASH5 LINC complex couples telomeres to microtubules during meiosis; SUN1 and SUN2 seem to act at least partial redundantly. Anchors chromosome movement in the prophase of meiosis and is involved in selective gene expression of coding and non-coding RNAs needed for gametogenesis. Required for telomere attachment to nuclear envelope and gametogenesis. May also function on endocytic vesicles as a receptor for RAB5-GDP and participate in the activation of RAB5.

gene.name: SUV39H1 histone lysine methyltransferase
gene.function: Histone methyltransferase that specifically mediates trimethylation of 'Lys-9' of histone H3 (H3K9me3) using monomethylated H3 'Lys-9' (H3K9me1) as substrate. Also weakly methylates histone H1 (in vitro). H3 'Lys-9' trimethylation represents a specific tag for epigenetic transcriptional repression by recruiting HP1 (CBX1, CBX3 and/or CBX5) proteins to methylated histones. Mainly functions in heterochromatin regions, thereby playing a central role in the establishment of constitutive heterochromatin at pericentric and telomere regions (By similarity). H3 'Lys-9' trimethylation is also required to direct DNA methylation at pericentric repeats. SUV39H1 is targeted to histone H3 via its interaction with RB1 and is involved in many processes, such as repression of MYOD1-stimulated differentiation, regulation of the control switch for exiting the cell cycle and entering differentiation, repression by the PML-RARA fusion protein, BMP-induced repression, repression of switch recombination to IgA and regulation of telomere length. Involved in the maintenance of H3K9me3 mark following DNA replication, when histone marks are diluted: HP1 recognizes the preexisting H3K9me3 mark and serves as a platform to recruit SUV39H1 to modify the adjacent newly incorporated histones. Component of the eNoSC (energy-dependent nucleolar silencing) complex, a complex that mediates silencing of rDNA in response to intracellular energy status and acts by recruiting histone- modifying enzymes. The eNoSC complex is able to sense the energy status of cell: upon glucose starvation, elevation of NAD(+)/NADP(+) ratio activates SIRT1, leading to histone H3 deacetylation followed by dimethylation of H3 at 'Lys-9' (H3K9me2) by SUV39H1 and the formation of silent chromatin in the rDNA locus. Recruited by the large PER complex to the E-box elements of the circadian target genes such as PER2 itself or PER1, contributes to the conversion of local chromatin to a heterochromatin- like repressive state through H3 'Lys-9' trimethylation (By similarity).

gene.name: toll like receptor 4
gene.function: Transmembrane receptor that functions as a pattern recognition receptor recognizing pathogen- and damage-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs and DAMPs) to induce innate immune responses via downstream signaling pathways. At the plasma membrane, cooperates with LY96 to mediate the innate immune response to bacterial lipopolysaccharide (LPS). Also involved in LPS- independent inflammatory responses triggered by free fatty acids, such as palmitate, and Ni(2+). Mechanistically, acts via MYD88, TIRAP and TRAF6, leading to NF-kappa-B activation, cytokine secretion and the inflammatory response. Alternatively, CD14-mediated TLR4 internalization via endocytosis is associated with the initiation of a MYD88-independent signaling via the TICAM1-TBK1-IRF3 axis leading to type I interferon production. In addition to the secretion of proinflammatory cytokines, initiates the activation of NLRP3 inflammasome and formation of a positive feedback loop between autophagy and NF-kappa-B signaling cascade. In complex with TLR6, promotes inflammation in monocytes/macrophages by associating with TLR6 and the receptor CD86. Upon ligand binding, such as oxLDL or amyloid-beta 42, the TLR4:TLR6 complex is internalized and triggers inflammatory response, leading to NF-kappa-B-dependent production of CXCL1, CXCL2 and CCL9 cytokines, via MYD88 signaling pathway, and CCL5 cytokine, via TICAM1 signaling pathway. In myeloid dendritic cells, vesicular stomatitis virus glycoprotein G but not LPS promotes the activation of IRF7, leading to type I IFN production in a CD14- dependent manner. Required for the migration-promoting effects of ZG16B/PAUF on pancreatic cancer cells.

gene.name: TNF superfamily member 11
gene.function: Cytokine that binds to TNFRSF11B/OPG and to TNFRSF11A/RANK. Osteoclast differentiation and activation factor. Augments the ability of dendritic cells to stimulate naive T-cell proliferation. May be an important regulator of interactions between T-cells and dendritic cells and may play a role in the regulation of the T-cell-dependent immune response. May also play an important role in enhanced bone-resorption in humoral hypercalcemia of malignancy. Induces osteoclastogenesis by activating multiple signaling pathways in osteoclast precursor cells, chief among which is induction of long lasting oscillations in the intracellular concentration of Ca (2+) resulting in the activation of NFATC1, which translocates to the nucleus and induces osteoclast-specific gene transcription to allow differentiation of osteoclasts. During osteoclast differentiation, in a TMEM64 and ATP2A2-dependent manner induces activation of CREB1 and mitochondrial ROS generation necessary for proper osteoclast generation (By similarity).

gene.name: tumor protein p53
gene.function: Multifunctional transcription factor that induces cell cycle arrest, DNA repair or apoptosis upon binding to its target DNA sequence. Acts as a tumor suppressor in many tumor types; induces growth arrest or apoptosis depending on the physiological circumstances and cell type. Negatively regulates cell division by controlling expression of a set of genes required for this process. One of the activated genes is an inhibitor of cyclin-dependent kinases. Apoptosis induction seems to be mediated either by stimulation of BAX and FAS antigen expression, or by repression of Bcl-2 expression. Its pro-apoptotic activity is activated via its interaction with PPP1R13B/ASPP1 or TP53BP2/ASPP2. However, this activity is inhibited when the interaction with PPP1R13B/ASPP1 or TP53BP2/ASPP2 is displaced by PPP1R13L/iASPP. In cooperation with mitochondrial PPIF is involved in activating oxidative stress-induced necrosis; the function is largely independent of transcription. Induces the transcription of long intergenic non-coding RNA p21 (lincRNA-p21) and lincRNA-Mkln1. LincRNA-p21 participates in TP53-dependent transcriptional repression leading to apoptosis and seems to have an effect on cell-cycle regulation. Implicated in Notch signaling cross-over. Prevents CDK7 kinase activity when associated to CAK complex in response to DNA damage, thus stopping cell cycle progression. Isoform 2 enhances the transactivation activity of isoform 1 from some but not all TP53-inducible promoters. Isoform 4 suppresses transactivation activity and impairs growth suppression mediated by isoform 1. Isoform 7 inhibits isoform 1-mediated apoptosis. Regulates the circadian clock by repressing CLOCK-BMAL1-mediated transcriptional activation of PER2.

gene.name: tumor protein p53 binding protein 1
gene.function: Double-strand break (DSB) repair protein involved in response to DNA damage, telomere dynamics and class-switch recombination (CSR) during antibody genesis. Plays a key role in the repair of double-strand DNA breaks (DSBs) in response to DNA damage by promoting non-homologous end joining (NHEJ)-mediated repair of DSBs and specifically counteracting the function of the homologous recombination (HR) repair protein BRCA1. In response to DSBs, phosphorylation by ATM promotes interaction with RIF1 and dissociation from NUDT16L1/TIRR, leading to recruitment to DSBs sites. Recruited to DSBs sites by recognizing and binding histone H2A monoubiquitinated at 'Lys-15' (H2AK15Ub) and histone H4 dimethylated at 'Lys-20' (H4K20me2), two histone marks that are present at DSBs sites. Required for immunoglobulin class- switch recombination (CSR) during antibody genesis, a process that involves the generation of DNA DSBs. Participates in the repair and the orientation of the broken DNA ends during CSR (By similarity). In contrast, it is not required for classic NHEJ and V(D)J recombination (By similarity). Promotes NHEJ of dysfunctional telomeres via interaction with PAXIP1.

gene.name: TSC complex subunit 2
gene.function: Catalytic component of the TSC-TBC complex, a multiprotein complex that acts as a negative regulator of the canonical mTORC1 complex, an evolutionarily conserved central nutrient sensor that stimulates anabolic reactions and macromolecule biosynthesis to promote cellular biomass generation and growth. Within the TSC-TBC complex, TSC2 acts as a GTPase- activating protein (GAP) for the small GTPase RHEB, a direct activator of the protein kinase activity of mTORC1. In absence of nutrients, the TSC-TBC complex inhibits mTORC1, thereby preventing phosphorylation of ribosomal protein S6 kinase (RPS6KB1 and RPS6KB2) and EIF4EBP1 (4E-BP1) by the mTORC1 signaling. The TSC-TBC complex is inactivated in response to nutrients, relieving inhibition of mTORC1. Involved in microtubule-mediated protein transport via its ability to regulate mTORC1 signaling (By similarity). Also stimulates the intrinsic GTPase activity of the Ras- related proteins RAP1A and RAB5 (By similarity).

gene.name: ubiquitin specific peptidase 18
gene.function: Interferon-induced ISG15-specific protease that plays a crucial role for maintaining a proper balance of ISG15-conjugated proteins in cells. Regulates protein ISGylation by efficiently cleaving ISG15 conjugates linked via isopeptide bonds. Acts as a negative regulator of cGAS-STING signaling be mediating deISGylation of CGAS. Regulates T-cell activation and T-helper 17 (Th17) cell differentiation by deubiquitinating TAK1, likely to keep TAK1-TAB complexes in steady conditions. In turn, restricts activation of NF-kappa-B, NFAT, and JNK as well as expression of IL2 in T-cells after TCR activation. Acts as a molecular adapter with USP20 to promote innate antiviral response through deubiquitinating STING1. Involved also in the negative regulation of the inflammatory response triggered by type I interferon. Upon recruitment by STAT2 to the type I interferon receptor subunit IFNAR2 interferes with the assembly of the ternary interferon-IFNAR1-IFNAR2 complex and acts as a negative regulator of the type I interferon signaling pathway.

gene.name: voltage dependent anion channel 1
gene.function: Non-selective voltage-gated ion channel that mediates the transport of anions and cations through the mitochondrion outer membrane and plasma membrane. The channel at the outer mitochondrial membrane allows diffusion of small hydrophilic molecules; in the plasma membrane it is involved in cell volume regulation and apoptosis. It adopts an open conformation at low or zero membrane potential and a closed conformation at potentials above 30-40 mV. The open state has a weak anion selectivity whereas the closed state is cation-selective. Binds various signaling molecules, including the sphingolipid ceramide, the phospholipid phosphatidylcholine, and the sterols cholesterol and oxysterol. In depolarized mitochondria, acts downstream of PRKN and PINK1 to promote mitophagy or prevent apoptosis; polyubiquitination by PRKN promotes mitophagy, while monoubiquitination by PRKN decreases mitochondrial calcium influx which ultimately inhibits apoptosis. May participate in the formation of the permeability transition pore complex (PTPC) responsible for the release of mitochondrial products that triggers apoptosis. May mediate ATP export from cells. Part of a complex composed of HSPA9, ITPR1 and VDAC1 that regulates mitochondrial calcium-dependent apoptosis by facilitating calcium transport from the ER lumen to the mitochondria intermembrane space thus providing calcium for the downstream calcium channel MCU that directly releases it into mitochondria matrix (By similarity). Mediates cytochrome c efflux.

gene.name: vitamin D receptor
gene.function: Nuclear receptor for calcitriol, the active form of vitamin D3 which mediates the action of this vitamin on cells. Enters the nucleus upon vitamin D3 binding where it forms heterodimers with the retinoid X receptor/RXR. The VDR-RXR heterodimers bind to specific response elements on DNA and activate the transcription of vitamin D3-responsive target genes. Plays a central role in calcium homeostasis (By similarity). Also functions as a receptor for the secondary bile acid lithocholic acid (LCA) and its metabolites.
gene.target_class: Nuclear hormone receptor subfamily 1 group I member 1

gene.name: exportin 1
gene.function: Mediates the nuclear export of cellular proteins (cargos) bearing a leucine-rich nuclear export signal (NES) and of RNAs. In the nucleus, in association with RANBP3, binds cooperatively to the NES on its target protein and to the GTPase RAN in its active GTP-bound form (Ran-GTP). Docking of this complex to the nuclear pore complex (NPC) is mediated through binding to nucleoporins. Upon transit of a nuclear export complex into the cytoplasm, disassembling of the complex and hydrolysis of Ran-GTP to Ran-GDP (induced by RANBP1 and RANGAP1, respectively) cause release of the cargo from the export receptor. The directionality of nuclear export is thought to be conferred by an asymmetric distribution of the GTP- and GDP-bound forms of Ran between the cytoplasm and nucleus. Involved in U3 snoRNA transport from Cajal bodies to nucleoli. Binds to late precursor U3 snoRNA bearing a TMG cap.

gene.name: zinc metallopeptidase STE24
gene.function: Transmembrane metalloprotease whose catalytic activity is critical for processing lamin A/LMNA on the inner nuclear membrane and clearing clogged translocons on the endoplasmic reticulum. Proteolytically removes the C- terminal three residues of farnesylated proteins. Also plays an antiviral role independently of its protease activity by restricting enveloped RNA and DNA viruses, including influenza A, Zika, Ebola, Sindbis, vesicular stomatitis, cowpox, and vaccinia. Mechanistically, controls IFITM antiviral pathway to hinder viruses from breaching the endosomal barrier by modulating membrane fluidity.

gene.name: zinc finger RANBP2-type containing 3
gene.function: DNA annealing helicase and endonuclease required to maintain genome stability at stalled or collapsed replication forks by facilitating fork restart and limiting inappropriate recombination that could occur during template switching events. Recruited to the sites of stalled DNA replication by polyubiquitinated PCNA and acts as a structure-specific endonuclease that cleaves the replication fork D-loop intermediate, generating an accessible 3'-OH group in the template of the leading strand, which is amenable to extension by DNA polymerase. In addition to endonuclease activity, also catalyzes the fork regression via annealing helicase activity in order to prevent disintegration of the replication fork and the formation of double-strand breaks.

papers.title: Lonafarnib: First Approval.
papers.summary: This review reports that lonafarnib, a selective farnesyltransferase inhibitor, was approved in the United States to reduce mortality risk in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome and treats processing-deficient progeroid laminopathies with specific LMNA or ZMPSTE24 variants. Mechanistic studies and phase 2 studies indicate reduced progerin farnesylation, improved nuclear defects, longer survival, and selected clinical improvements, although substantial gastrointestinal toxicity and null benefit from adding pravastatin and zoledronic acid were observed.
papers.why: Reports the clinical development and FDA approval of lonafarnib for reducing mortality in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome and related progeroid laminopathies.

papers.title: Progerin Expression Induces Inflammation, Oxidative Stress and Senescence in Human Coronary Endothelial Cells.
papers.summary: In primary human coronary artery endothelial cells, adenoviral progerin overexpression induced endothelial dysfunction, including inflammation, oxidative stress, persistent DNA double-strand breaks, cell-cycle arrest, and cellular senescence, whereas wild-type prelamin A did not. The pravastatin–zoledronate combination partly rescued these abnormalities by inhibiting progerin prenylation, but the study was performed exclusively in an in vitro overexpression model with higher progerin levels than occur in patients.
papers.why: The endothelial-cell model shows that pravastatin plus zoledronate partially prevents progerin-induced vascular dysfunction and senescence.

papers.title: Progerinin, an optimized progerin-lamin A binding inhibitor, ameliorates premature senescence phenotypes of Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome.
papers.summary: The paper identifies progerinin (SLC-D011), a progerin–lamin A binding inhibitor, and shows that it reduces progerin abundance, reverses senescence-associated cellular changes, and improves premature-aging phenotypes and survival in HGPS patient-derived fibroblasts and LmnaG609G mouse models. Intraperitoneal and oral administration were effective, with oral progerinin generally producing greater anti-aging effects than intraperitoneal treatment and showing stronger cellular and mouse survival effects than lonafarnib in the reported experiments.
papers.why: Reports an optimized small-molecule progerin-lamin A inhibitor that extends lifespan, improves body weight, and ameliorates histological and physiological disease phenotypes in progeria mice.

papers.title: Presence and distribution of progerin in HGPS cells is ameliorated by drugs that impact on the mevalonate and mTOR pathways.
papers.summary: In AG01972 primary HGPS fibroblasts, indirect immunofluorescence showed that FTI-277, pravastatin, zoledronic acid, rapamycin, and N-acetyl-L-cysteine increased the proportion of cells without detectable progerin, while only some treatments redistributed or eliminated internal progerin speckles. FTI-277, pravastatin, and FTI-277 plus GGTI-2133 produced the strongest restoration of lamin A nuclear-rim distribution, all tested treatments improved lamin B2 distribution, and drugs that blocked farnesylation often accumulated uncleaved prelamin A at the nuclear rim.
papers.why: The study directly tests multiple mevalonate- and mTOR-pathway drugs in HGPS cells and measures progerin and nuclear-lamin distribution.

papers.title: A Tissue Engineered Blood Vessel Model of Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome Using Human iPSC-derived Smooth Muscle Cells.
papers.summary: The study developed a human iPSC-derived smooth-muscle-cell tissue-engineered blood vessel model of Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome that reproduced reduced vasoactivity, medial-wall thickening, calcification, apoptosis, and abnormal cellularity. Everolimus improved vasoactivity, contractile-marker expression, and nuclear morphology while reducing progerin expression, but it did not reverse established calcification or apoptosis.
papers.why: The tissue-engineered vascular model reproduces HGPS vascular defects and demonstrates response to everolimus.

papers.title: Epigenetic clock for skin and blood cells applied to Hutchinson Gilford Progeria Syndrome and ex vivo studies.
papers.summary: The paper develops a 391-CpG DNA methylation age estimator, the skin & blood clock, that detects accelerated epigenetic aging in fibroblasts from patients with Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome, whereas the pan-tissue clock does not. The clock also tracks proliferation-associated aging in cultured human cells and supports use as an ex vivo assay for screening compounds that alter epigenetic aging.
papers.why: The newly validated epigenetic age assay detects accelerated aging in HGPS fibroblasts and quantifies aging dynamics in cultured human cells.

papers.title: Recapitulation of premature ageing with iPSCs from Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome.
papers.summary: Reprogramming HGPS patient fibroblasts into induced pluripotent stem cells eliminated progerin and reset HGPS-associated nuclear, epigenetic, and gene-expression abnormalities, whereas differentiation restored progerin and premature smooth-muscle-cell senescence. Progerin perturbation experiments identified progerin as a key driver of senescence and loss of the DNAPK holoenzyme, while HGPS-iPSC-derived smooth muscle cells provide an in vitro model of premature and physiological vascular aging.
papers.why: Creates HGPS iPSCs that erase progerin-associated defects and restore vascular aging phenotypes after differentiation, offering a reusable disease and screening model.

papers.title: In vivo base editing rescues Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome in mice.
papers.summary: This paper shows that an LMNA-targeted adenine base editor, delivered by lentivirus in HGPS patient-derived fibroblasts or dual AAV9 in a transgenic mouse model, corrects the pathogenic c.1824 C>T mutation, reduces progerin RNA and protein, and improves cellular, vascular, adiposity, vitality, and lifespan phenotypes. Off-target DNA or RNA editing was not detected in the analyzed patient-derived cells, while mouse follow-up identified liver tumors associated with rare AAV integration as a potential safety concern requiring further study.
papers.why: Adenine base editing directly corrected the pathogenic LMNA allele in patient fibroblasts and HGPS mice, reducing progerin and vascular pathology while substantially extending mouse lifespan.

papers.title: Chromatin histone modifications and rigidity affect nuclear morphology independent of lamins.
papers.summary: The paper shows that loss of heterochromatin and reduced chromatin-based nuclear rigidity contribute to abnormal nuclear morphology in progerin-expressing cells and Hutchinson–Gilford progeria syndrome patient cells. The broad histone demethylase inhibitor methylstat increased heterochromatin and nuclear rigidity and markedly reduced nuclear irregularity and blebbing in the progerin model and patient cells, but these were in-vitro findings without testing of clinical disease outcomes.
papers.why: Increasing heterochromatin with histone demethylase inhibitors rescued nuclear morphology in HGPS cell lines and patient cells, identifying a pharmacologically actionable approach.

papers.title: The mutant form of lamin A that causes Hutchinson-Gilford progeria is a biomarker of cellular aging in human skin.
papers.summary: The paper shows that the LMNA G608G mutation causes aberrant progerin splicing in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome and that progerin accumulates markedly with cellular age in HGPS fibroblasts. In unaffected human skin, low-level progerin transcripts occur at all ages, while progerin protein increases with age in dermal fibroblasts and a small subset of terminally differentiated keratinocytes, supporting progerin as a biomarker of cellular aging.
papers.why: The study directly validates abnormal progerin expression in HGPS skin and shows that progerin accumulation can serve as a biomarker of cellular aging.

papers.title: Remodeling of Bone Marrow Hematopoietic Stem Cell Niches Promotes Myeloid Cell Expansion during Premature or Physiological Aging.
papers.summary: In the LmnaG609G/G609G progeroid mouse model, premature myeloid-biased hematopoiesis was primarily associated with remodeling of the bone marrow microenvironment rather than HSC-autonomous LMNA dysfunction. Chronic treatment with the β3-adrenergic receptor agonist BRL37344 normalized peripheral lineage skewing, reduced excessive long-term HSCs, and restored proximity between HSCs and megakaryocytes.
papers.why: β3-adrenergic receptor agonism in progeroid mice reduces pathological myeloid and stem-cell expansion and restores hematopoietic niche organization.

papers.title: Nucleolar expansion and elevated protein translation in premature aging.
papers.summary: In patient-derived HGPS fibroblasts, progerin expression is associated with rDNA de-repression, enlarged and more active nucleoli, increased ribosome biogenesis, and elevated global protein translation rather than broadly increased protein degradation. Nucleolar size and activity increase with physiological aging, supporting nucleolar size as a candidate aging biomarker, while the study identifies regulation of ribosome biogenesis as a possible therapeutic target.
papers.why: The study identifies increased ribosome biogenesis and expanded nucleoli in HGPS cells and proposes nucleolar size and activity as measurable aging biomarkers.

papers.title: Small Extracellular Vesicles Have GST Activity and Ameliorate Senescence-Related Tissue Damage.
papers.summary: Small extracellular vesicles from young-donor fibroblasts partially ameliorated senescence-associated phenotypes in four HGPS patient-derived fibroblast lines, including proliferation arrest and elevated p16INK4A and p21CIP1. Mechanistic experiments linked part of this activity to vesicle-associated GSTM2, glutathione conjugation, reduced reactive oxygen species, and reduced lipid peroxidation, but the study did not test treatment in patients with HGPS.
papers.why: Young-donor extracellular vesicles improve senescence-associated phenotypes in HGPS cells and old tissues, identifying a regenerative therapy and measurable response markers.

papers.title: Targeting of NAT10 enhances healthspan in a mouse model of human accelerated aging syndrome.
papers.summary: Chemical inhibition of NAT10 with Remodelin or genetic Nat10 haploinsufficiency improved healthspan and multiple cardiovascular, nuclear, and genomic phenotypes in homozygous and heterozygous LmnaG609G mouse models of Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome. The study also identifies acetylated α-tubulin K40 as a potential target-engagement readout, while complete Nat10 deletion is embryonic lethal and no human efficacy was established.
papers.why: NAT10 inhibition or depletion enhances healthspan in an HGPS mouse model and extends the findings beyond farnesylation-based approaches.

papers.title: Methionine Restriction Extends Lifespan in Progeroid Mice and Alters Lipid and Bile Acid Metabolism.
papers.summary: Methionine restriction extended health span and median lifespan by approximately 20–21% in two progeroid mouse models, while attenuating inflammatory, DNA-damage, lipid-metabolism, and bile-acid alterations. A 0.1% cholic-acid-enriched diet independently improved health span and median lifespan in Zmpste24−/− progeroid mice, supporting bile-acid metabolism as a potential intervention target.
papers.why: Demonstrates that methionine restriction and cholic acid improve health span and lifespan in two mouse models of HGPS.

papers.title: MG132-induced progerin clearance is mediated by autophagy activation and splicing regulation.
papers.summary: In HGPS patient-derived cells, MG132 reduced progerin through complementary autophagy-dependent clearance and altered LMNA splicing, while improving nuclear morphology, senescence, proliferation, viability, and gene-expression abnormalities. Progerin and SRSF-1 also decreased after local MG132 injection in Lmna G609G/G609G mouse muscle, but systemic treatment did not significantly reduce progerin and would require improved delivery for multi-organ use.
papers.why: The study demonstrates in HGPS cells and progeria mice that MG132 reduces progerin through autophagy and splicing regulation while improving cellular phenotypes.

papers.title: Development of a CRISPR/Cas9-based therapy for Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome.
papers.summary: The paper shows that CRISPR/Cas9 disruption of LMNA exon 11 reduces progerin and lamin A, ameliorates nuclear abnormalities and multiple phenotypes, and extends survival in the LmnaG609G/G609G mouse model of Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome. Editing and progerin reduction were demonstrated in patient-derived fibroblasts, but in vivo delivery was tissue-limited, especially in the aorta, and the consequences of permanently abolishing lamin A in humans remain unknown.
papers.why: The study developed a CRISPR/Cas9 strategy that introduced corrective LMNA frameshifts and reversed multiple HGPS cellular and mouse disease alterations.

papers.title: Vascular Smooth Muscle-Specific Progerin Expression Accelerates Atherosclerosis and Death in a Mouse Model of Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome.
papers.summary: The paper establishes two atherosclerosis-prone mouse models of Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome and shows that progerin expression restricted to vascular smooth muscle cells, but not macrophages, is sufficient to accelerate atherosclerosis, produce vulnerable plaques, and shorten lifespan. The data identify progerin-induced loss of vascular smooth muscle cells, increased medial LDL retention, and plaque destabilization as key mechanisms of vascular disease in these models.
papers.why: The study directly develops several HGPS mouse models and quantitative cardiovascular assays that reproduce progerin-induced atherosclerosis and premature death.

papers.title: Depleting the methyltransferase Suv39h1 improves DNA repair and extends lifespan in a progeria mouse model.
papers.summary: Prelamin A/progerin binds and stabilizes SUV39H1, elevates the heterochromatic mark H3K9me3, and is linked to defective DNA repair and accelerated senescence in progeria models. Depleting Suv39h1 reduced DNA-damage foci and senescence and improved body weight, bone mineral density, and lifespan in Zmpste24-null mice, with a median survival increase from 23 to 37 weeks.
papers.why: SUV39H1 loss experimentally restored DNA repair, delayed senescence, improved bone density, and extended lifespan by about 60% in a progeria mouse model.

papers.title: Rescue of heterochromatin organization in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria by drug treatment.
papers.summary: In fibroblasts from three Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome patients carrying the G608G LMNA mutation, progerin accumulation was associated with age-dependent nuclear-shape defects, heterochromatin loss, altered transcript distribution, and reduced transcriptional activity. Sequential treatment with the farnesyl-transferase inhibitor mevinolin and the histone deacetylase inhibitor trichostatin A markedly lowered progerin and restored nuclear heterochromatin, transcript organization, ribonucleoprotein staining, and aspects of nuclear shape in vitro.
papers.why: Combined mevinolin and trichostatin A treatment lowered progerin and restored heterochromatin and transcript organization in cultured HGPS fibroblasts.

papers.title: Single-dose CRISPR-Cas9 therapy extends lifespan of mice with Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome.
papers.summary: This study shows that systemic, single-dose delivery of AAV9-packaged CRISPR/Cas9 guide RNAs targeting Lmna reduces lamin A/progerin and improves health-related phenotypes and lifespan in a homozygous progerin G609G mouse model of Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome. Benefits were modest and incomplete, with editing concentrated mainly in the liver and acute megacolon/megacaecum-associated lethality in some treated mice.
papers.why: Single-dose systemic CRISPR-Cas9 editing reduced lamin A/progerin and extended lifespan in an HGPS mouse model.

papers.title: A Cell-Intrinsic Interferon-like Response Links Replication Stress to Cellular Aging Caused by Progerin.
papers.summary: Progerin causes replication-fork stalling and MRE11-dependent degradation, accompanied by genomic instability and a cell-intrinsic, interferon-independent STAT1-regulated IFN-like response that contributes to poor cellular fitness in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome. Calcitriol and other compounds that improve HGPS cellular phenotypes reduce replication stress and STAT1 signaling, while calcitriol also increases cellular reprogramming efficiency.
papers.why: The study shows that calcitriol and other phenotypic rescue compounds reduce progerin-associated replication stress and the interferon-like response while improving HGPS cell fitness.

papers.title: Endothelial progerin expression causes cardiovascular pathology through an impaired mechanoresponse.
papers.summary: The paper shows that endothelial progerin expression causes impaired shear-stress mechanosensing, reduced endothelial nitric oxide synthase and nitric oxide, and MRTFA-dependent profibrotic signaling, leading to cardiac fibrosis, hypertrophy, diastolic dysfunction, and premature death in an endothelium-specific HGPS mouse model. MRTFA inhibition rescued endothelial nitric oxide synthase levels and nearly abolished the profibrotic effect of progerin-expressing endothelial cells on fibroblasts in vitro, although the mouse model did not reproduce vascular smooth muscle cell loss.
papers.why: An endothelium-specific progerin mouse model reproduces HGPS cardiovascular pathology, and MRTFA inhibition rescues eNOS expression and reduces profibrotic effects in vitro.

papers.title: Inhibition of DNA damage response at telomeres improves the detrimental phenotypes of Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome.
papers.summary: The study identifies progerin-induced transcription of telomeric non-coding RNAs and consequent telomeric DNA damage response activation as a causal contributor to proliferative defects, cellular senescence, pathological skin remodeling, inflammation, and shortened survival in HGPS models. Sequence-specific telomeric antisense oligonucleotides reduce these abnormalities in cultured human cells and improve skin homeostasis and lifespan in a transgenic HGPS mouse model, without correcting heterochromatin loss, altered nuclear shape, or progerin expression.
papers.why: Telomeric antisense oligonucleotides inhibited progerin-induced DNA-damage signaling and premature senescence in HGPS patient cells while improving skin homeostasis and lifespan in an HGPS mouse model.

papers.title: Cytoskeleton stiffness regulates cellular senescence and innate immune response in Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome.
papers.summary: The paper reports that progeria cells exhibit coupled increases in cytoskeletal stiffness, RhoA/ROCK and Sun2 signaling, nuclear blebbing and micronuclei-associated cGAS–Sting activation, together with cellular senescence and impaired muscle stem-cell function. RhoA/ROCK inhibition with Y-27632 reduced these abnormalities in Zmpste24−/− muscle-derived mesenchymal stromal/stem cells and human HGPS fibroblasts, while systemic treatment improved skeletal-muscle regeneration in Zmpste24−/− mice.
papers.why: RhoA/ROCK inhibition reduced cytoskeletal stiffness, senescence, and innate immune signaling in HGPS cells and improved muscle regeneration in a progeria mouse model.

papers.title: iPSC-Derived Endothelial Cells Affect Vascular Function in a Tissue-Engineered Blood Vessel Model of Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome.
papers.summary: Patient-derived iPSC endothelial and smooth muscle cells were incorporated into a three-dimensional tissue-engineered blood vessel model that reproduced HGPS-associated vascular inflammation, structural abnormalities, progerin expression, and impaired vasoactivity. Experiments assigning healthy or HGPS cell sources independently showed that HGPS endothelial cells directly reduced vasodilation and induced VCAM-1 and E-selectin expression in the engineered vessels.
papers.why: This study develops an HGPS-specific patient iPSC vascular model and quantifies endothelial dysfunction and cardiovascular biomarkers under flow.

papers.title: Generation of a Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome monkey model by base editing.
papers.summary: This study generated cynomolgus monkeys carrying the pathogenic LMNA 1824 C>T (Gly608Gly) mutation using BE4max base editing and showed that the resulting animals expressed progerin and recapitulated major HGPS phenotypes. The model reproduced growth failure, alopecia, loss of subcutaneous fat, craniofacial and skeletal abnormalities, reduced mobility, cellular senescence, inflammation, and early aortic disease, while comprehensive newborn-monkey sequencing found no detectable genome-wide off-target editing effect.
papers.why: Base editing produced monkeys carrying the HGPS LMNA mutation that expressed progerin and reproduced human growth, skeletal, and vascular phenotypes.

papers.title: The JAK1/2 inhibitor ruxolitinib delays premature aging phenotypes.
papers.summary: Ruxolitinib inhibits JAK1/2-dependent progerin-induced senescence in human fibroblasts and improves several premature-aging phenotypes in Zmpste24−/− mice, including rib fractures, grip strength, bone mineral content, and a trend toward longer survival. The findings provide preclinical proof of concept for ruxolitinib in Hutchinson–Gilford progeria syndrome, but efficacy in patients remains untested and reported safety risks require consideration.
papers.why: Ruxolitinib rescued progerin-associated cellular senescence and nuclear abnormalities in human cells while improving skeletal, muscle, and survival phenotypes in a mouse model.

papers.title: mtDNA release promotes cGAS-STING activation and accelerated aging of postmitotic muscle cells.
papers.summary: In Zmpste24−/− mouse myofibers modeling Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome, the paper links oxidative mtDNA damage and increased VDAC1 oligomerization to cytosolic mtDNA release, dysfunctional mitophagy, cGAS-STING and NF-κB activation, and increased senescence-associated secretory phenotype expression. The VDAC1 oligomerization inhibitor VBIT4 reduced cGAS-STING signaling and SASP-factor expression in cultured progeria myofibers, while nuclear DNA damage was not detectably increased.
papers.why: In a Zmpste24-deficient progeria mouse model, VBIT4 reduces mtDNA release, cGAS-STING activation, and SASP expression.

papers.title: Prelamin A causes progeria through cell-extrinsic mechanisms and prevents cancer invasion.
papers.summary: The study shows that ZMPSTE24-deficient, prelamin A-accumulating cells can coexist with normal cells without overt progeria, indicating that cell-extrinsic mechanisms are predominant in progeria pathogenesis. Wild-type cells and extracellular matrix rescued deficient-cell proliferation in vitro, supporting systemic, cell-based, gene-correction, and extracellular-matrix-related research strategies; separately, ZMPSTE24 silencing reduced invasion in human cancer cells.
papers.why: The study develops a progerin-accumulating mosaic mouse model and experimentally demonstrates a cell-extrinsic mechanism of progeria while testing ZMPSTE24 silencing.

papers.title: Vitamin D receptor signaling improves Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome cellular phenotypes.
papers.summary: In HGPS patient-derived fibroblasts, progerin accumulation and lamin A/C depletion are associated with reduced vitamin D receptor signaling, depletion of DNA-repair factors, DNA damage, abnormal nuclear morphology, and premature senescence. Prolonged treatment with 1α,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3 restored VDR, BRCA1, and 53BP1, reduced progerin and DNA damage, improved nuclear morphology, and delayed senescence, but the experiments were conducted in vitro.
papers.why: The study directly tests vitamin D3/VDR restoration in HGPS patient-derived cells and improves progeria-associated nuclear, DNA-repair, and senescence phenotypes.

papers.title: Defective lamin A-Rb signaling in Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome and reversal by farnesyltransferase inhibition.
papers.summary: Patient-derived HGPS fibroblasts showed a broad defect in lamin A-Rb signaling, including decreased RB1 expression and altered networks governing the cell cycle, DNA replication and repair, differentiation, and survival. Three days of 1.5 µM lonafarnib normalized 288 of 352 abnormally expressed genes, leaving 99% of genes expressed at levels comparable to lonafarnib-treated control fibroblasts, with less than 2% cell death under the tested conditions.
papers.why: Directly demonstrates that farnesyltransferase inhibition reverses lamin A-Rb signaling defects in patient HGPS fibroblasts.

papers.title: METTL3 counteracts premature aging via m6A-dependent stabilization of MIS12 mRNA.
papers.summary: In isogenic LMNA-mutant HGPS and WRN-knockout human mesenchymal stem cell models, reduced METTL3 expression, diminished N6-methyladenosine (m6A) methylation, and destabilized MIS12 mRNA were associated with premature cellular senescence. METTL3 overexpression increased global m6A, restored proliferative capacity, reduced SA-β-Gal staining, and mechanistically stabilized MIS12 mRNA through IGF2BP2 in HGPS and Werner syndrome cells.
papers.why: Shows that restoring the METTL3–m6A–MIS12 pathway rescues senescence in human mesenchymal stem-cell models of progeroid syndromes.

papers.title: Everolimus rescues multiple cellular defects in laminopathy-patient fibroblasts.
papers.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
papers.summary: In primary fibroblasts from patients with HGPS and five other LMNA-associated laminopathies, 0.1 μM everolimus reduced the mTOR-inhibition biomarker pRPS6, improved proliferation in all six laminopathy lines, and eliminated detectable senescence-associated β-galactosidase staining after 2 weeks. Nuclear morphology improved significantly in three of four laminopathy lines with nuclear blebbing, but overall lamin A/C abundance did not decrease, and the proposed autophagy mechanism could not be tested because autophagy inhibitors were excessively toxic.
papers.why: Everolimus improves proliferation, senescence, and nuclear morphology in fibroblasts from multiple LMNA-related laminopathies, including HGPS-related disease models.

papers.title: Generation and characterization of a novel knockin minipig model of Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome.
papers.summary: The paper generated heterozygous LMNA c.1824C > T Yucatan minipigs that endogenously express progerin and recapitulate the growth, cutaneous, skeletal, cardiovascular, renal, testicular, and early-death phenotypes of Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome. The animals also developed reduced myocardial perfusion, myocardial and vascular fibrosis, cardiac dysfunction, electrical abnormalities, and vascular smooth muscle loss, while their human-like size and cardiovascular anatomy support use for translational device, imaging, and therapy studies.
papers.why: The minipig reproduces major HGPS phenotypes and provides a large-animal platform and cardiovascular readouts for testing therapies and devices.

papers.title: Transient introduction of human telomerase mRNA improves hallmarks of progeria cells.
papers.summary: Transient introduction of active human telomerase hTERT mRNA selectively improved telomere length, proliferation, senescence-associated phenotypes, and nuclear morphology in HGPS fibroblasts with short telomeres, whereas catalytically inactive hTERT did not. Combining hTERT mRNA with lonafarnib enhanced proliferation, but hTERT did not restore H3K9me3 under the tested transient-expression conditions, and the findings remain in vitro rather than clinical evidence.
papers.why: Transient hTERT mRNA improves telomere length, proliferation, lifespan, senescence markers, and nuclear morphology in HGPS cells, with enhanced proliferation when combined with lonafarnib.

papers.title: Genetic reduction of mTOR extends lifespan in a mouse model of Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria syndrome.
papers.summary: A double-copy C57BL/6J LMNA G608G transgenic mouse model recapitulated major skin, adipose, skeletal, vascular, and premature-aging phenotypes of Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome. Heterozygous reduction of Mtor partially restored vascular smooth muscle cells, normalized S6K activity in newborn fibroblasts, and extended mouse lifespan by 30%, but it did not reduce progerin abundance, restore nuclear membrane structure, rescue growth deficiency or adventitial expansion, and increased embryonic lethality.
papers.why: Genetic reduction of mTOR extends lifespan in a mouse model that recapitulates multiple HGPS phenotypes and directly supports testing pharmacologic mTOR inhibition.

papers.title: SAMMY-seq reveals early alteration of heterochromatin and deregulation of bivalent genes in Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome.
papers.summary: The paper introduces SAMMY-seq and shows that it can map lamina-associated heterochromatin in primary cells without crosslinking, antibodies, or transgene expression. Applied to early-passage HGPS fibroblasts, the method reveals patient-specific chromatin accessibility changes, preserved H3K9me3-dependent silencing, altered H3K27me3 distribution, and transcriptional dysregulation of a subset of Polycomb-regulated bivalent genes.
papers.why: SAMMY-seq provides a high-throughput method that directly identifies early chromatin changes in HGPS fibroblasts and related molecular markers.

papers.title: An inhibitory role of progerin in the gene induction network of adipocyte differentiation from iPS cells.
papers.summary: Patient-derived HGPS induced pluripotent stem cells differentiated through either embryoid bodies or mesenchymal stem cells reproduced severe adipocyte lipid-storage failure, nuclear blebbing, binucleation, and premature senescence. Progerin suppressed induction of the terminal adipogenic regulators PPARγ2 and C/EBPα while largely sparing the early regulators C/EBPβ and C/EBPδ, identifying a differentiation-stage-specific mechanism underlying HGPS lipodystrophy.
papers.why: Two patient-specific iPSC differentiation approaches reproducibly model HGPS lipodystrophy and identify progerin-mediated repression of terminal adipogenesis.

papers.title: Reduction of senescent fibro-adipogenic progenitors in progeria-aged muscle by senolytics rescues the function of muscle stem cells.
papers.summary: In the Zmpste24−/− mouse model of Hutchinson–Gilford progeria syndrome, senescent fibro-adipogenic progenitors were associated with reduced muscle stem/progenitor-cell numbers and impaired proliferation and myogenesis. The senolytic fisetin selectively induced apoptosis in senescent FAPs, restored MPC function in vitro, and improved FAP abundance, fibrosis, myofibre size, and muscle strength in vivo.
papers.why: Fisetin reduced senescent fibro-adipogenic progenitors in progeria-aged muscle and improved muscle stem-cell function, providing a tested therapeutic strategy for progeria-related muscle disease.

papers.title: Progeria: a rare genetic premature ageing disorder.
papers.summary: This review summarizes the molecular basis, experimental models, diagnostic approaches, and therapeutic candidates for Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome. It reports that lonafarnib improved weight gain and cardiovascular and skeletal manifestations in children, while model studies also support farnesyltransferase inhibition, SUN1 reduction, IGF-1 treatment, and splice correction; no definitive early-detection biomarker or diagnostic kit was available.
papers.why: Describes clinically tested lonafarnib and the available experimental progeroid models for studying HGPS pathology and treatment effects.

papers.title: Drug screening on Hutchinson Gilford progeria pluripotent stem cells reveals aminopyrimidines as new modulators of farnesylation.
papers.summary: The paper reports a high-throughput screen of 21 608 small molecules in HGPS iPSC-derived mesenchymal stem cells. Monoaminopyrimidines, including Mono-AP1, Mono-AP2 and Mono-AP3, inhibited farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase and farnesyl transferase, rescued nuclear-shape abnormalities and premature osteogenic differentiation, and showed less cytostatic activity than tipifarnib in vitro.
papers.why: A 21,608-compound screen using HGPS pluripotent stem cells identified aminopyrimidines that inhibit farnesylation and rescue HGPS-associated in-vitro phenotypes.

papers.title: Progerin expression disrupts critical adult stem cell functions involved in tissue repair.
papers.summary: In non-immortalized human MIAMI marrow stromal cells, progerin overexpression impaired nuclear integrity, self-renewal marker expression and localization, proliferation, migration, and membrane elasticity, providing mechanistic links to impaired vascular repair in HGPS. FTI-277 ameliorated several—but not necessarily all—of these abnormalities, indicating partial rescue by farnesyltransferase inhibition.
papers.why: The study directly models progerin-mediated stem-cell defects and reports that farnesyltransferase inhibition ameliorates several defects in progerin-expressing cells.

papers.title: Rapamycin Rescues Age-Related Changes in Muscle-Derived Stem/Progenitor Cells from Progeroid Mice.
papers.summary: In muscle-derived stem/progenitor cells from Zmpste24−/− progeroid mice, hyperactivated mTORC1 was associated with apoptosis, senescence, impaired myogenic and chondrogenic differentiation, reduced osteogenic differentiation, and enhanced adipogenic differentiation. Rapamycin lowered mTORC1 activity and improved apoptosis, senescence, myogenic differentiation, chondrogenic differentiation, and adipogenic imbalance, but did not restore proliferation or significantly improve osteogenic differentiation.
papers.why: Rapamycin improves differentiation, senescence, apoptosis, and regenerative defects in progeroid mouse cells through a mechanistically relevant mTORC1 pathway.

papers.title: The Senolytic Drug Fisetin Attenuates Bone Degeneration in the Zmpste24 -/- Progeria Mouse Model.
papers.summary: In the Zmpste24−/− mouse model of Hutchinson–Gilford progeria syndrome, four weekly doses of fisetin reduced kidney senescence-associated transcripts and attenuated age-associated bone-density loss. Dasatinib plus quercetin and 17-DMAG showed little or no protection from trabecular bone loss, while both dasatinib plus quercetin and fisetin reduced senescence in cultured musculoskeletal cells.
papers.why: This study directly tests senolytic drugs in a Zmpste24−/− progeria mouse model and reports that fisetin reduces age-associated bone loss.

papers.title: p300 nucleocytoplasmic shuttling underlies mTORC1 hyperactivation in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome.
papers.summary: The paper shows that progerin mislocalizes p300, increases mTORC1 activity and suppresses autophagy in Hutchinson–Gilford progeria syndrome (HGPS) cells. In patient-derived fibroblasts, p300 inhibition with A485, AMPK activation with 991, or CRM1 inhibition with selinexor alleviated selected HGPS phenotypes, although the effects of 991 and selinexor on H3K9me3 depended on p300 shuttling.
papers.why: The study identifies a disease-specific p300-mTORC1-autophagy mechanism and shows that modulating p300 shuttling normalizes progerin-associated cellular phenotypes.

papers.title: Dose imbalance of DYRK1A kinase causes systemic progeroid status in Down syndrome by increasing the un-repaired DNA damage and reducing LaminB1 levels.
papers.summary: This paper identifies a transferable progeroid mechanism in Down syndrome: DYRK1A overdose and kinase activity cause excess unrepaired DNA double-strand breaks, reduced Lamin B1, senescence, and reduced cerebral-organoid cortical folding. It explicitly links these findings to the Lamin B1 depletion and B-type laminopathy characteristic of Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome, while showing that DYRK1A inhibitors harmine and ID8 correct selected DNA-damage and senescence phenotypes in Down syndrome cell models; no treatment effect in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome was tested.
papers.why: In the progeroid phenotype of Down syndrome, pharmacological correction with kinase inhibitors was demonstrated in patient-relevant hiPSCs and cerebral organoids, while IgG glycans provided an accelerated-aging biomarker.

papers.title: <i>ZMPSTE24</i> missense mutations that cause progeroid diseases decrease prelamin A cleavage activity and/or protein stability.
papers.summary: The paper develops a humanized Saccharomyces cerevisiae system that directly measures human ZMPSTE24-dependent cleavage of human prelamin A and shows that all eight tested disease-associated ZMPSTE24 missense variants have reduced processing, with defects attributable to catalytic activity, protein stability, or both. Deletion of DOA10 or proteasome inhibition with bortezomib restores processing for the unstable P248L and W340R variants, suggesting a mutation-specific therapeutic strategy that requires validation in patient cells and patients.
papers.why: The humanized yeast system directly tests disease-associated ZMPSTE24 variants from progeroid disorders and identifies bortezomib-mediated rescue for stability-defective mutants.

papers.title: Targeting the phospholipase A2 receptor ameliorates premature aging phenotypes.
papers.summary: The study identifies PLA2R1 as a mediator of progerin-induced cellular senescence and nuclear-shape abnormalities, with evidence from progerin-expressing human fibroblasts, HGPS patient-derived fibroblasts, and Zmpste24-deficient mice. PLA2R1 inhibition reduced senescence and some bone-aging phenotypes through a pathway involving p53 and FDPS, while pamidronate, an FDPS inhibitor, reduced senescence and misshapen nuclei in progerin-expressing cells.
papers.why: PLA2R1 inhibition or knockout and the FDPS inhibitor pamidronate reduced senescence and progeria-associated cellular or skeletal phenotypes in HGPS patient cells and mice.

papers.title: Phase I Study of Progerinin in Healthy Volunteers
papers.summary: PRG-PRO-001 is a Phase I, Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-Controlled, Single Ascending Dose (SAD) Study including a food interaction study, followed by a Multiple Ascending Dose (MAD) Study to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamic Profile of Progerinin in Healthy Volunteers. This is a first-in-human study. The study aims to determine the safety and tolerability of Progerinin after single and multiple doses in healthy volunteers and to evaluate the pharmacokinetics (PK) of Progerinin after single and multiple dose administrations in healthy volunteers.

papers.title: Study of Zoledronic Acid, Pravastatin, and Lonafarnib for Patients With Progeria
papers.summary: Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome (Progeria) is a rare autosomal disease that results in premature death at a median age of 13 years due to cardiovascular and cerebralvascular compromise. The mutation for this disease has been identified and results in a mutant form of lamin A that cannot be de-farnesylated. This study evaluates the combination of pravastain (a statin), lonafarnib (a farnesyltransferase inhibitor) and zoledronic acid (a bisphosphonate) in an open label phase II efficacy trial in children with Progeria. These agents all target farnesylation pathways at different points. Pati

papers.title: Phase II Trial of Lonafarnib (a Farnesyltransferase Inhibitor) for Progeria
papers.summary: This is an open label dose adjusted phase II trial of the oral farnesyltransferase inhibitor (FTI) lonafarnib (SCH66336) for patients with HGPS and progeroid laminopathies.

papers.title: Treatment of the Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome With a Combination of Pravastatin and Zoledronic Acid
papers.summary: We suggest treating the Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome by two molecules (zoledronic acid and pravastatin).The therapeutic approach which we propose has for objectives to reduce, to prevent or to delay the gravest infringements of the disease, to prolong the life of the children, and in a more general way, aim at improving their living conditions.

papers.title: Phase I/II Trial of Everolimus in Combination With Lonafarnib in Progeria
papers.summary: This is a phase I/II dose-escalation trial of everolimus in combination with lonafarnib in Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome (HGPS) and progeroid laminopathies (henceforth "progeria"). The study will be conducted at a single clinical site utilizing the Clinical and Translational Study Unit (CTSU) at Boston Children's Hospital. Lonafarnib will be administered at doses previously established in the pediatric population and in this population of progeria subjects. This study will first determine the dose-limiting toxicities (DLT) and the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) of everolimus when administ

papers.title: Study to Determine Optimal Dose and Evaluate Safety, Tolerability, and Pharmacokinetics of Progerinin in Patients With Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome (HGPS)
papers.summary: Researchers will compare treatment with progerinin plus lonafarnib vs lonafarnib alone to assess optimal dosing, safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics in patients with Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome (HGPS). Subjects in the randomized study arms will continue to take the standard of care (SOC), lonafarnib, and will be randomized to either take SOC alone or in combination with progerinin.

papers.title: Umbilical Cord Blood Transfusion in Progeria Syndrome
papers.summary: This is a pilot study on safety and efficacy of umbilical cord blood therapy for patients with Hutchinson Gilford Progeria syndrome (HGPS). This is an 1 year trial with 3 IV infusions (4 months apart from each infusion) of umbilical cord blood units with oral Sirolimus to see the safety and efficacy.

papers.title: A Study of Zoledronic Acid, Pravastatin, and Lonafarnib for Patients With Progeria
papers.summary: This is an open label single arm feasibility trial. A combination of two oral agents (pravastatin and lonafarnib) and one intravenous (IV) agent (zoledronic acid) will be administered at doses and schedule currently applied in pediatrics. These agents all target farnesylation pathways at different points. Our goal is to inhibit farnesylation of abnormal lamin, the disease-causing protein in Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome and progeroid laminopathies (henceforth "progeria"). The drugs will include the intravenous bisphosphonate zoledronic acid, oral HMG co-reductase inhibitor pravastatin a

papers.title: Open Targets drug and clinical candidates for Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome
Open Targets drugs acting on FDPS
Metformin Suppresses Cancer Stem Cells through AMPK Activation and Inhibition of Protein Prenylation of the Mevalonate Pathway in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.summary: This paper reports that metformin suppresses colorectal cancer stem cells in cell and xenograft models by activating AMPK, inhibiting mTOR signaling, and repressing the mevalonate pathway, including decreased FDPS expression. Mevalonate reverses metformin-mediated FDPS suppression and cancer stem cell reduction, while direct inhibition of farnesylation or geranylgeranylation reduces the stem-cell population; these findings provide an experimentally supported transfer mechanism involving FDPS/protein prenylation.

papers.title: FDPS cooperates with PTEN loss to promote prostate cancer progression through modulation of small GTPases/AKT axis.
papers.summary: This study shows that FDPS is overexpressed in PTEN-deficient prostate cancer and promotes cell growth, proliferation, and oncogenic signaling through increased prenylation of Rho A, Rho G, and CDC42 and activation of AKT/ERK. Zoledronic acid (ZOL) reduced FDPS expression, small-GTPase prenylation, colony formation, proliferation, and 3D tumoroid growth in PTEN-deficient prostate cancer models, but efficacy varied across cell types and the findings are preclinical rather than demonstrated in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome.

papers.title: Nebulization of risedronate alleviates airway obstruction and inflammation of chronic obstructive pulmonary diseases via suppressing prenylation-dependent RAS/ERK/NF-κB and RhoA/ROCK1/MLCP signaling.
papers.summary: In cigarette-smoke/elastase or LPS-induced rodent COPD models, nebulized risedronate inhibited FDPS-dependent RAS and RhoA prenylation, suppressed downstream contractile and inflammatory signaling, and improved airway obstruction and lung inflammation. The study provides evidence that risedronate acts on the FDPS mechanism relevant to Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome, but it did not test Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome models or patients.

papers.title: Influence of Nutrient (NPK) Factors on Growth, and Pharmacodynamic Component Biosynthesis of Atractylodes chinensis: An Insight on Acetyl-CoA Carboxylase (ACC), 3-Hydroxy-3-Methylglutaryl-CoA Reductase (HMGR), and Farnesyl Pyrophosphate Synthase (FPPS) Signaling Responses.
papers.summary: Field experiments in Atractylodes chinensis showed that high-phosphorus NPK fertilization, especially the T3 and T6 schemes, increased rhizome FPPS activity and FPPS gene expression and was associated with increased volatile-oil accumulation. The paper concerns the plant enzyme farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase (FPPS), not the human disease mechanism FDPS or Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome, so it provides only an indirect plant-system precedent.

papers.title: Nitrogen-containing bisphosphonate induces enhancement of OPG expression and inhibition of RANKL expression via inhibition of farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase to inhibit the osteogenic differentiation and calcification in vascular smooth muscle cells.
papers.summary: In rat A7r5 vascular smooth muscle cells, zoledronic acid inhibited β-glycerophosphate-induced osteogenic differentiation and calcification by increasing OPG and decreasing RANKL, with downstream rescue experiments implicating FDPS pathway inhibition. The evidence is in vitro, FPPS dependence was inferred using downstream metabolites rather than measured directly, and the paper notes that clinical studies had not demonstrated protection against human vascular calcification.

papers.title: Towards an Improvement of Anticancer Activity of Benzyl Adenosine Analogs.
papers.summary: This paper identifies the FPPS enzyme, corresponding to the requested FDPS mechanism, as a target of N6-benzyladenosine derivatives in colorectal cancer models. Compound 2f impaired RAS and Rap-1A prenylation, linking this biochemical effect to FPPS inhibition, although 2f did not materially reduce viability or proliferation in the tested cell lines; other derivatives produced antiproliferative or cytotoxic effects that were not exclusively attributable to FDPS inhibition.

papers.title: Drug repositioning of mevalonate pathway inhibitors as antitumor agents for ovarian cancer.
papers.summary: The study shows that inhibitors of the mevalonate pathway, particularly the farnesyltransferase inhibitor lonafarnib and the geranylgeranyltransferase inhibitor GGTI-298, concentration-dependently inhibited SKOV3 and OVCAR5 ovarian cancer cell growth and induced autophagy markers. Alendronate also inhibited ovarian cancer cell growth in vitro and reduced tumor burden in mogp-TAg mice, supporting drug repositioning of mevalonate-pathway inhibitors; the paper does not directly study progerin farnesylation or Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome.
papers.why: Experimental drug-repositioning data show that inhibiting the mevalonate/prenylation pathway suppresses tumor-cell growth and induces autophagy, providing a mechanistically transferable strategy for progerin farnesylation.

papers.title: Uncovering protein prenylation in Th1 cells: novel prenylation sites and insights into statin and farnesyltransferase inhibition.
papers.summary: In primary in vitro-differentiated Th1 cells, click-chemistry enrichment and mass spectrometry identified broad, activation-dependent protein prenylation and showed that FTI-277 reduced farnesylation of 49 proteins, including Lamin A, while Pitavastatin produced distinct and partly opposing effects on farnesylation and geranylgeranylation. For transfer to Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome, the paper provides mechanistic background linking progerin farnesylation to the disease and reviews Lonafarnib as an approved farnesyltransferase inhibitor, but it does not test interventions in progeria or progerin.
papers.why: The study provides experimentally validated prenylation-profiling methods and evidence that statin/prenyltransferase perturbation alters the prenylome, which is transferable to progerin farnesylation biology.

papers.title: Synergistic Suppression of NF1 Malignant Peripheral Nerve Sheath Tumor Cell Growth in Culture and Orthotopic Xenografts by Combinational Treatment with Statin and Prodrug Farnesyltransferase Inhibitor PAMAM G4 Dendrimers.
papers.summary: A water-soluble PAMAM G4 dendrimer prodrug farnesyltransferase inhibitor, IG 2, combined with low-dose lovastatin synergistically inhibited RAS- and prenylation-dependent proliferation of NF1 malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor cells and markedly suppressed established xenograft growth. The intervention broadly reduced farnesylation and geranylgeranylation, showed no additive or synergistic antiproliferative effect in several normal cell models, and was not tested on progerin farnesylation or Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome.

papers.title: Squalene synthase induces ERα expression via cholesterol supplementation to confer statin resistance in lung cancer cells.
papers.summary: This paper shows that SQS/FDFT1 overexpression in lung cancer cells increases lovastatin resistance by replenishing cholesterol and increasing ERα protein expression, while SQS or ERα inhibition restores sensitivity. The study does not mention or test progerin farnesylation or Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome.

papers.title: IL-33-mediated mast cell and eosinophil function requires isoprenylation.
papers.summary: The paper shows that inhibiting protein isoprenylation through simvastatin or the dual farnesyltransferase/geranylgeranyltransferase-1 inhibitor FGTI-2734 suppresses IL-33-mediated mast-cell and eosinophil functions, with FGTI-2734 also reducing inflammatory-cell influx in a mouse peritonitis model. These findings provide experimentally supported inhibitors of the farnesylation/prenylation machinery relevant to progerin farnesylation, but the study does not test Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome, progerin, or a progeria model.

papers.title: Statins decrease Toll-like receptor 4 expression and downstream signaling in human CD14+ monocytes.
papers.summary: In human CD14+ monocytes, simvastatin and atorvastatin reduced TLR4 expression and downstream inflammatory signaling by inhibiting protein geranylgeranylation and farnesylation. The study did not examine progerin or progerin farnesylation, so its relevance to Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome is mechanistic rather than disease-specific.

papers.title: Everolimus suppresses glucose transporter 3 membrane trafficking to improve therapeutic efficacy of umbilical cord blood-derived mesenchymal stem cell transplantation in diabetic retinopathy.
papers.summary: In diabetic retinopathy models, everolimus inhibits mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 signaling in hyperglycemia-exposed human umbilical cord blood-derived mesenchymal stem cells, reducing GLUT3 membrane trafficking, glucose influx, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, and cell death. Everolimus-pretreated cells improved retinal function and photoreceptor-layer thickness after subconjunctival transplantation in streptozotocin-induced diabetic rats, while rapamycin was less effective under the tested conditions.

papers.title: Rapamycin-nanoliposomes target the mTORC1-mediated autophagy-lysosomal and NLRP3/Caspase-1 pathways to inhibit nucleus pulposus cell senescence in intervertebral discs.
papers.summary: Rapamycin-loaded nanoliposomes suppressed IL-1β-associated nucleus pulposus cell senescence by inhibiting mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 phosphorylation, thereby inhibiting the NLRP3/Caspase-1 pathway and enhancing autophagy–lysosomal function. The formulation also reduced IL-1β-induced intervertebral disc degeneration in rats, although effects on other cells and long-term safety remain unresolved.

papers.title: Impaired Chaperone-Mediated Autophagy Accelerates Intervertebral Disc Degeneration by Inducing MIDN Accumulation to Target TSC2 for Proteasomal Degradation.
papers.summary: This study identifies an impaired chaperone-mediated autophagy–MIDN–TSC2 axis in intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD), resulting in hyperactivation of mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) and downstream senescence, SASP, and extracellular matrix degradation. In rat nucleus pulposus cell and caudal needle-puncture models, rapamycin directly inhibited mTORC1 and reduced degenerative phenotypes, providing transferable evidence for pharmacologic mTORC1 rescue.

papers.title: Exosome-targeted injectable hydrogels for sustained DEPTOR delivery and delay of IDD via the mTORC1/SASP pathway.
papers.summary: This study developed an exosome-containing OSA/CMCS injectable hydrogel for sustained delivery of DEPTOR and evaluated it in a puncture-induced rat model of intervertebral disc degeneration. The hydrogel reduced inflammation and slowed degeneration, supporting the DEPTOR/mTORC1/SASP pathway as a therapeutic target.

papers.title: Rapamycin and nicotinamide treatment attenuates senescence-associated features in mesenchymal stromal cells isolated from elderly donors by modulating autophagy.
papers.summary: Short-term in vitro treatment of mesenchymal stromal cells from elderly donors with rapamycin and nicotinamide partially attenuated senescence-associated changes and improved osteogenic differentiation. The treatment effects were associated with altered mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 activity and modulation of autophagy, but their in vivo relevance and long-term stability remain unconfirmed.

papers.title: Inhalable mucus-penetrating and senescence-targeted nanoliposomes reverse senescence to overcome chemoresistance for enhanced lung cancer therapy.
papers.summary: The paper reports that inhalable L1CAM-targeted nanoliposomes co-encapsulating rapamycin and doxorubicin reverse therapy-induced senescence in chemoresistant lung cancer cells. In a chemoresistant lung cancer mouse model, inhalation suppressed tumor growth without appreciable systemic toxicity by inhibiting the mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTOR), reversing senescence, increasing autophagy, and resensitizing cancer cells to chemotherapy.

papers.title: MRE11 inhibition highlights a replication stress-dependent vulnerability of MYCN-driven tumors.
papers.summary: The paper shows that MRE11 restrains replication stress and DNA damage in MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma cells, creating a vulnerability to MRE11 inhibition. The MRE11 inhibitor mirin increased replication stress, activated the DNA damage response, and caused p53-dependent apoptosis and tumor-growth suppression in preclinical cell and xenograft models, with possible harm in non-MYCN-driven models.

papers.title: Mre11 exonuclease activity promotes irreversible mitotic progression under replication stress.
papers.summary: In a Xenopus egg-extract system, Mre11 exonuclease activity promotes replication-stress-associated mitotic entry and mitotic replisome disassembly by facilitating early processing of stalled replication forks. Mirin suppresses these outcomes, whereas Wee1/Myt1 inhibition or a nonphosphorylatable CDK1 mutant partially bypasses the requirement for Mre11, although recovery is incomplete.

papers.title: Discovery of new inhibitors of nuclease MRE11.
papers.summary: MU147 and MU1409 are newly identified, relatively specific inhibitors of MRE11 nuclease that impair MRE11-dependent double-strand break repair and nascent-strand degradation at stalled replication forks. Their effect is selective for BRCA2-deficient cells, but it leaves ATM activation intact; the paper presents the compounds as chemical probes and potential therapeutic leads rather than reporting clinical efficacy.

papers.title: GRB2 stabilizes RAD51 at reversed replication forks suppressing genomic instability and innate immunity against cancer.
papers.summary: This paper shows that GRB2 protects reversed replication forks by binding RAD51, inhibiting RAD51 ATPase activity, and limiting MRE11-mediated fork degradation; the MRE11 inhibitor mirin rescues replication-fork degradation in GRB2-deficient cells. In a metastatic ovarian cancer model, GRB2 depletion combined with the PARP inhibitor talazoparib enhanced immune activation, reduced tumor burden and ascites, and prolonged survival.

papers.title: ASPM promotes ATR-CHK1 activation and stabilizes stalled replication forks in response to replication stress.
papers.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
papers.summary: ASPM is a RAD17-dependent scaffold that loads RAD9 and TopBP1 at stalled replication forks, activates the ATR-CHK1 checkpoint, and suppresses MRE11-mediated nascent-DNA degradation. ASPM-deficient cells and mouse neural progenitor cells therefore show stalled-fork stabilization defects and increased degradation under replication stress, while MRE11 inhibition rescues the nascent-DNA degradation phenotype in cells.

papers.title: The linker histone H1-BRCA1 axis is a crucial mediator of replication fork stability.
papers.summary: The study identifies replication-dependent histone H1 variants as chromatin factors that recruit BRCA1 to stalled replication forks and protect nascent DNA from MRE11-dependent resection. Hydroxyurea-induced replication stress, BRCA1 loss, or histone H1 depletion causes fork deprotection, DNA breaks, genomic instability, and reduced cell survival, while the MRE11 inhibitor MIRIN suppresses fork resection when histone H1 is depleted.

papers.title: IFN-γ Facilitates Corneal Epithelial Cell Pyroptosis Through the JAK2/STAT1 Pathway in Dry Eye.
papers.summary: This paper shows that IFN-γ activates the JAK2/STAT1 pathway in experimental dry eye and promotes NLRP3 inflammasome-associated pyroptosis in corneal epithelial cells. Pharmacologic inhibition with fludarabine, STAT1-targeting siRNA, IFN-γ neutralization, or ROS scavenging with N-acetylcysteine reduced pyroptosis-related changes and improved ocular-surface outcomes, providing transferable intervention strategies for diseases involving the STAT1-regulated interferon-like response.

papers.title: Neuroinflammatory disease signatures in SPG11-related hereditary spastic paraplegia patients.
papers.summary: In SPG11-related hereditary spastic paraplegia, IFNγ produces excessive STAT1 signaling, inflammatory cytokine and chemokine release, phagocytosis, and microglia-conditioned-media neurotoxicity. The JAK inhibitor ruxolitinib suppressed STAT1/CXCL10 activation and prevented the associated increase in neuronal cell death, supporting transfer of this mechanism as an intervention target for interferon-driven disorders.

papers.title: A novel stop-loss variant in ISG15 causes C-terminal dysfunction and impairs USP18-mediated negative feedback.
papers.summary: A child with compound heterozygous ISG15 variants had persistent type I interferon signaling, increased p-STAT1, reduced ISGylation, and inflammatory skin and liver manifestations. Baricitinib attenuated interferon-related molecular signals and improved the patient's ulcerative skin lesions, providing a transferable intervention against the STAT1-regulated interferon-like response.

papers.title: Neuropathologic Impacts of JAK Inhibitor Treatment in Aicardi-Goutières Syndrome.
papers.summary: This letter describes profound cerebral atrophy, diminished white matter, and extensive intracranial calcifications after more than four years of baricitinib treatment in a patient with Aicardi-Goutières syndrome. Although JAK inhibitors block downstream effects of type I interferon activation, the case indicates that prolonged early treatment did not prevent severe central nervous system sequelae and motivates options with enhanced CNS bioavailability.

papers.title: Augmented PFKFB3-mediated glycolysis by interferon-γ promotes inflammatory M1 polarization through the JAK2/STAT1 pathway in local vascular inflammation in Takayasu arteritis.
papers.summary: In Takayasu arteritis, IFN-γ increased PFKFB3-dependent glycolysis and inflammatory M1 macrophage polarization through JAK2/STAT1 signaling. PFK-015, tofacitinib, baricitinib, and fludarabine suppressed metabolic, signaling, phenotypic, or inflammatory readouts in patient-derived macrophages, identifying the STAT1-regulated interferon-like response as a potentially transferable intervention mechanism.

papers.title: IFN‑γ induces apoptosis in human melanocytes by activating the JAK1/STAT1 signaling pathway.
papers.summary: In primary human epidermal melanocytes, IFN-γ activated JAK1/STAT1 signaling, altered pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins, reduced proliferation, and increased apoptosis.
