Pretreatment with the STAT1 inhibitor fludarabine significantly reduced IFN-γ-induced apoptosis, supporting JAK1/STAT1 signaling as a potentially targetable mediator of melanocyte loss relevant to vitiligo.

unread.title: The farnesyl transferase inhibitor (FTI) lonafarnib improves nuclear morphology in ZMPSTE24-deficient fibroblasts from patients with the progeroid disorder MAD-B.
unread.why: Lonafarnib corrects abnormal nuclear morphology in ZMPSTE24-deficient progeroid fibroblasts that share progerin-processing defects with HGPS.

unread.title: Clinical Trial of the Protein Farnesylation Inhibitors Lonafarnib, Pravastatin, and Zoledronic Acid in Children With Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome.
unread.why: This HGPS clinical trial directly tested triple therapy and reported weight, vascular, and bone-mineral-density outcomes.

unread.title: Impact of farnesylation inhibitors on survival in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome.
unread.why: The study establishes an HGPS natural-history survival benchmark and reports a substantial survival benefit associated with protein-farnesylation inhibitor treatment.

unread.title: Impact of miR-181a on SIRT1 Expression and Senescence in Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome.
unread.why: miR-181a-5p inhibition restores SIRT1, increases proliferation, and reduces senescence in HGPS fibroblasts with supporting mouse-model evidence.

unread.title: FDA approval summary for lonafarnib (Zokinvy) for the treatment of Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome and processing-deficient progeroid laminopathies.
unread.why: The FDA summary reports up to 11 years of follow-up showing an approximately 2.5-year survival advantage with lonafarnib.

unread.title: Ghrelin delays premature aging in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome.
unread.why: Ghrelin reduces progerin and senescence in HGPS cells while improving lipodystrophy, weight loss, histopathology, and lifespan in a mouse model.

unread.title: Phenotype and course of Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome.
unread.why: This longitudinal HGPS study defines reusable clinical and outcome measures and provides limited data showing growth benefits from growth-hormone treatment.

unread.title: LMNA-associated cardiocutaneous progeria: an inherited autosomal dominant premature aging syndrome with late onset.
unread.why: The study directly shows that farnesyltransferase inhibitors rescue abnormal nuclear morphology in fibroblasts from an LMNA-associated progeria syndrome sharing progerin-related pathology.

unread.title: Precise progerin targeting using RfxCas13d: A therapeutic avenue for Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome.
unread.why: The study demonstrates selective RfxCas13d knockdown of progerin mRNA and reversal of cellular and progeroid phenotypes in HGPS cells and mice.

unread.title: Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome mice display accelerated arterial thrombus formation and increased platelet reactivity.
unread.why: This HGPS mouse study provides a disease-relevant thrombosis model, quantitative platelet and coagulation endpoints, and data supporting antiplatelet intervention research.

unread.title: Nicotinamide Mononucleotide Alleviates Aging Defects in Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome.
unread.why: The study directly shows that NMN improves mitochondrial, DNA-damage, gonadal, cardiovascular, skin, and lifespan phenotypes in HGPS-derived cells and mice.

unread.title: An infant with congenital micrognathia and upper airway obstruction was diagnosed as Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome caused by a novel LMNA mutation: Case report and literature review.
unread.why: The case documents successful surgical relief of severe upper-airway obstruction in an infant with HGPS and molecular confirmation by a novel LMNA variant.

unread.title: Systematic screening identifies therapeutic antisense oligonucleotides for Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome.
unread.why: A systematic ASO screen and in vivo validation identified an optimized progerin-reducing oligonucleotide that extended lifespan in an HGPS mouse model.

unread.title: Hutchinson-Gilford progeria patient-derived cardiomyocyte model of carrying LMNA gene variant c.1824 C > T.
unread.why: The paper develops and validates HGPS patient-derived iPSC-cardiomyocytes that exhibit structural, contractile, and gene-expression defects relevant to cardiomyopathy.

unread.title: Adenine base editing rescues pathogenic phenotypes in tissue engineered vascular model of Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome.
unread.why: Adenine base editing corrected the pathogenic LMNA mutation in HGPS cells and improved vascular smooth-muscle density, vasodilation, fibrosis, and mouse lifespan-related outcomes.

unread.title: Plasma Progerin in Patients With Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome: Immunoassay Development and Clinical Evaluation.
unread.why: The study developed and clinically evaluated a plasma progerin assay that distinguishes HGPS patients, tracks lonafarnib response, and relates progerin reduction to survival.

unread.title: Clinical trial of a farnesyltransferase inhibitor in children with Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome.
unread.why: A clinical trial of lonafarnib in children with HGPS showed improvement in growth-related and vascular or skeletal outcomes, providing direct evidence for an existing treatment.

unread.title: Association of Lonafarnib Treatment vs No Treatment With Mortality Rate in Patients With Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome.
unread.why: A matched cohort study found lower mortality among children with HGPS receiving oral lonafarnib than among untreated controls, although the observational design limits causal interpretation.

unread.title: Anti-hsa-miR-59 alleviates premature senescence associated with Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome in mice.
unread.why: AAV9 anti-miR-59 treatment reduced fibrosis and aging-related tissue phenotypes and increased lifespan by 25.5% in an HGPS mouse model.

unread.title: Impact of Combined Baricitinib and FTI Treatment on Adipogenesis in Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome and Other Lipodystrophic Laminopathies.
unread.why: Baricitinib alone or combined with a farnesyltransferase inhibitor improved adipocyte differentiation and lipid-droplet formation in HGPS patient-derived cells and related lipodystrophy models.

unread.title: The secretome atlas of two mouse models of progeria.
unread.why: The study profiled circulating proteins in two progeria models, identified candidate biomarkers and therapeutic targets, and developed a proteomic age-acceleration predictor.

unread.title: Selection of specific and efficient siRNAs in new cellular model for Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome therapy.
unread.why: Selected siRNAs reduced progerin without reducing lamin A/C, showed additive activity with lonafarnib, and worked across three patient fibroblast lines.

unread.title: A non-canonical cGAS-STING pathway drives cellular and organismal aging.
unread.why: Pharmacological inhibition of the non-canonical cGAS-STING pathway ameliorated aging hallmarks, reduced tissue degeneration, and extended lifespan in progeria mice, while vitamin D receptor activation rescued canonical pathway responsiveness.

unread.title: Reversal of the cellular phenotype in the premature aging disease Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome.
unread.why: A splice-site-targeting oligonucleotide eliminated mutant LMNA products and reversed nuclear, chromatin, and gene-expression abnormalities in HGPS fibroblasts.

unread.title: MicroRNAs in hereditary and sporadic premature aging syndromes and other laminopathies.
unread.why: The review reports experimental evidence that miR-9 prevents progerin accumulation in HGPS neurons, providing a concrete therapeutic strategy for further testing.

unread.title: Laminopathies' Treatments Systematic Review: A Contribution Towards a 'Treatabolome'.
unread.why: The study systematically extracts and structures variant-specific treatments and phenotypic associations across LMNA-related diseases, including progeroid syndromes.

unread.title: Development of an accelerated cellular model for early changes in Alzheimer's disease.
unread.why: The study experimentally creates a rapid Alzheimer cellular model by adding progerin to familial-AD neural progenitors and validates disease phenotypes suitable for drug screening.

unread.title: Cellular Biomechanic Impairment in Cardiomyocytes Carrying the Progeria Mutation: An Atomic Force Microscopy Investigation.
unread.why: The study provides an experimentally characterized progeria-mutation cardiomyocyte model and quantitative assays for contractile and arrhythmogenic phenotypes relevant to HGPS cardiac disease.

unread.title: Aging Model for Analyzing Drug-Induced Proarrhythmia Risks Using Cardiomyocytes Differentiated from Progeria-Patient-Derived Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells.
unread.why: The paper validates progeria-derived cardiomyocytes as a disease-specific platform for detecting increased drug-induced proarrhythmia susceptibility.

unread.title: Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonism Prevents Type 2 Familial Partial Lipodystrophy Brown Adipocyte Dysfunction.
unread.why: Spironolactone redirected abnormal brown-adipocyte differentiation in LMNA-related FPLD2 and benefited an affected patient, providing a plausible treatment for transferable lamin A-related adipose dysfunction.

unread.title: The Accumulation of Progerin Underlies the Loss of Aortic Smooth Muscle Cells in Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome.
unread.why: The study directly uses HGPS and comparison mouse models to show that progerin accumulation, reduced AKT activity, and loss of aortic smooth muscle cells drive arterial pathology.

unread.title: Indirect bypass for revascularization in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome: an illustrative case.
unread.why: A pediatric HGPS patient achieved neoangiogenesis and improved perfusion after indirect cerebral bypass, demonstrating a cautiously applicable surgical strategy for disease-related hypoperfusion.

unread.title: STING causes replication stress and nascent DNA degradation via SAMHD1.
unread.why: SAMHD1 knockdown phenocopies STING loss in progeria cells and rescues replication-fork defects, identifying an experimentally supported therapeutic target for progerin-associated genome instability.

unread.title: Treatment with a farnesyltransferase inhibitor improves survival in mice with a Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome mutation.
unread.why: A farnesyltransferase inhibitor improved survival, body weight, and spontaneous fractures in an HGPS mutant mouse model, directly supporting this therapeutic strategy.

unread.title: Farnesyltransferase inhibition in HGPS.
unread.why: The article identifies FDA-approved Zokinvy as an effective HGPS therapy that blocks lamin A farnesylation and improves vascular and survival outcomes.

unread.title: Mutation-Agnostic Base Editing of the Progerin Farnesylation Site Rescues Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome Phenotypes in Neuromuscular Organoids
unread.why: The study develops and experimentally validates FATE in HGPS organoids, showing selective progerin elimination, restoration of DNA-repair foci and heterochromatin, and phenotypic rescue.

unread.title: Mutation-Agnostic Base Editing of the Progerin Farnesylation Site Rescues Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome Phenotypes in Neuromuscular Organoids
unread.why: This preprint reports experimental rescue of multiple HGPS phenotypes by transient, mutation-independent FATE delivery in patient-relevant neuromuscular organoids.

unread.title: Attenuating LRRK2 activity ameliorates progerin-induced aging phenotypes in HGPS models and during physiological aging
unread.why: The study identifies LRRK2 inhibition or opposing-phosphatase expression as interventions that ameliorate progerin-related aging defects in cells, worms, and aged cells.

unread.title: Genomic splice-donor disruption rescues systemic disease in progeria
unread.why: The study experimentally demonstrates splice-site editing that suppresses toxic progerin, preserves lamin A/C, reduces multiorgan pathology, and prolongs survival in progeroid mice.

unread.title: Increased Telomere Mobility in Progeria is Restored by Isoprenylcysteine Carboxyl Methyltransferase Inhibition
unread.why: The work establishes a quantitative telomere-mobility assay and shows partial rescue with lonafarnib and complete rescue with C75 in HGPS fibroblasts.

unread.title: The Anaphase Promoting Complex targets the toxic protein Progerin for ubiquitin-dependent degradation via autophagy
unread.why: The study identifies APC/CDC20-mediated autophagy as a degradative route for progerin and provides cellular assays showing that APC stimulation clears progerin and reduces nuclear blebs.

unread.title: Targeted ATAC-see (tATAC-see): A Visual Assay for Target-Specific Chromatin Profiling
unread.why: The study validates a tunable visual chromatin assay and demonstrates its ability to detect lamin-associated chromatin remodeling in HGPS aging models.

unread.title: Healing of chromosomal breaks is impeded in cells expressing progerin
unread.why: The study develops a progerin-expressing cellular assay that quantifies DNA end-joining defects and provides a reusable experimental system for HGPS DNA-repair research.

unread.title: Lonafarnib Partially Reverses Cardiac Senescence in Human and Mouse Progeria Models via Autophagy Activation
unread.why: The study tests repurposable drugs in HGPS patient-derived cardiomyocytes and progeroid mice, showing autophagy activation and partial reversal of cardiac senescence with lonafarnib.

unread.title: Improved Arterial Stiffness and Bone Mineral Density in Hutchinson–Gilford Progeria Treated with Bone Marrow-Derived Mesenchymal Stem Cells: A Case Study and Literature Review
unread.why: A case study reports tested intravenous MSC therapy with improved body composition, bone mineral density, arterial stiffness, growth, and inflammatory measures in HGPS.

unread.title: Intervention for Critical Aortic Stenosis in Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome
unread.why: The paper evaluates disease-specific interventions for critical aortic stenosis using four HGPS cases and reports three successful procedures and one perioperative death.

unread.title: MT-Exo-derived miR-4651 and miR-6126 coordinately regulate the SRSF1-progerin and SP1-PrPᶜ axes to attenuate vascular aging in HGPS.
unread.why: The study provides patient-anchored preclinical evidence that extracellular vesicles and their miRNAs reduce vascular dysfunction and progerin-associated abnormalities in HGPS models.

unread.title: Identification of mitochondrial dysfunction in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome through use of stable isotope labeling with amino acids in cell culture.
unread.why: Using patient fibroblasts and progeroid mouse models, the study identifies mitochondrial dysfunction and shows restoration with isoprenylation inhibitors tested clinically in HGPS.

unread.title: Neurologic features of Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome after lonafarnib treatment.
unread.why: A phase II/retrospective treatment study provides clinical outcome data suggesting lonafarnib improves neurologic manifestations in children with HGPS.

unread.title: A humanized yeast system to analyze cleavage of prelamin A by ZMPSTE24.
unread.why: The paper describes validated yeast-based assays for ZMPSTE24 and LMNA lamin-processing variants relevant to HGPS and related progeroid diseases.

unread.title: Inhibiting farnesylation reverses the nuclear morphology defect in a HeLa cell model for Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome.
unread.why: The HeLa cellular model demonstrates that pharmacologic or genetic inhibition of farnesylation reverses progerin-associated nuclear morphology defects.

unread.title: Mechanisms of premature vascular aging in children with Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome.
unread.why: The study establishes noninvasive cardiovascular measurements that characterize HGPS vasculopathy and can serve as longitudinal treatment-response outcome measures.

unread.title: Cardiac electrical defects in progeroid mice and Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome patients with nuclear lamina alterations.
unread.why: Provides experimentally validated HGPS-relevant mouse and cardiac assays linking progeria to measurable conduction abnormalities and connexin43 mislocalization in patients.

unread.title: Farnesyltransferase inhibitor and rapamycin correct aberrant genome organisation and decrease DNA damage respectively, in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome fibroblasts.
unread.why: Tests multiple HGPS drug regimens in patient-derived fibroblasts and shows that farnesyltransferase inhibitor combinations restore nuclear chromosome organization while rapamycin improves DNA-damage repair.

unread.title: Isoprenylcysteine Carboxylmethyltransferase-Based Therapy for Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome.
unread.why: Develops an ICMT inhibitor that improves multiple cellular, systemic, and cardiovascular HGPS phenotypes in patient cells and progeroid mice.

unread.title: Progerin-expressing endothelial cells are unable to adapt to shear stress.
unread.why: Establishes a shear-stress endothelial-cell assay and shows that lonafarnib and methystat improve stress adaptation in progerin-expressing and ZMPSTE24-deficient cells.

unread.title: Lonafarnib and everolimus reduce pathology in iPSC-derived tissue engineered blood vessel model of Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome.
unread.why: Tests lonafarnib and everolimus, alone and together, in a patient-derived HGPS blood-vessel microphysiological system and reports cardiovascular and vascular improvements.

unread.title: A noncanonical cGAS-STING pathway drives cellular and organismal aging.
unread.why: Identifies a noncanonical cGAS-STING aging pathway in progeria and reports pathway inhibition and vitamin D receptor activation as interventions that improve aging phenotypes and extend progeria-mouse lifespan.

unread.title: A small-molecule ICMT inhibitor delays senescence of Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome cells.
unread.why: Shows that genetic or pharmacological ICMT inhibition delays senescence, stimulates proliferation, improves survival, and restores vascular smooth muscle cells in HGPS models.

unread.title: SerpinE1 drives a cell-autonomous pathogenic signaling in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome.
unread.why: Identifies SerpinE1/PAI-1 as an HGPS disease effector and shows that pharmacological or genetic inhibition reverses multiple pathological features in patient-derived fibroblasts.

unread.title: Transcriptional activation of endogenous Oct4 via the CRISPR/dCas9 activator ameliorates Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome in mice.
unread.why: Demonstrates CRISPR/dCas9-mediated Oct4 activation as a therapeutic rejuvenation strategy that suppresses progerin accumulation, rescues vascular pathology, and extends lifespan in HGPS mice.

unread.title: Small-Molecule Therapeutic Perspectives for the Treatment of Progeria.
unread.why: Reviews established and developing small-molecule treatment strategies for HGPS, including the FDA-approved farnesyltransferase inhibitor lonafarnib.

unread.title: Lonafarnib improves cardiovascular function and survival in a mouse model of Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome.
unread.why: Provides preclinical evidence that lonafarnib improves arterial biomechanics, cardiac function, and survival in a mouse model of HGPS.

unread.title: Ankyrin G overexpression in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome fibroblasts identified through biological filtering of expression profiles.
unread.why: Develops and validates an expression-screening strategy identifying increased ankyrin G as a measurable molecular feature of HGPS fibroblasts.

unread.title: Doxycycline decelerates aging in progeria mice.
unread.why: Doxycycline extends lifespan and improves multiple progeroid phenotypes in Zmpste24-deficient mice, with effects also demonstrated in HGPS fibroblasts.

unread.title: Abnormal nuclear morphology is independent of longevity in a zmpste24-deficient fish model of Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome (HGPS).
unread.why: This paper generates and characterizes a zmpste24-deficient medaka model that reproduces selected HGPS-associated nuclear and telomere abnormalities.

unread.title: Intervention for critical aortic stenosis in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome.
unread.why: The study evaluates modified TAVR and apico-aortic conduit procedures in HGPS patients with critical aortic stenosis and reports clinical outcomes.

unread.title: Baricitinib and Lonafarnib Synergistically Target Progerin and Inflammation, Improving Lifespan and Health in Progeria Mice.
unread.why: Combined baricitinib and lonafarnib improves lifespan, progeroid phenotypes, vascular pathology, and inflammatory or senescent markers in HGPS mice.

unread.title: Cell immortalization facilitates prelamin A clearance by increasing both cell proliferation and autophagic flux.
unread.why: The study shows that immortalizing Zmpste24-deficient cells increases prelamin A clearance through proliferation and autophagy-related mechanisms, suggesting a targetable approach.

unread.title: Mesenchymal Stem Cell Therapy for Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria: Improvements in Arterial Stiffness and Bone Mineral Density in a Single Case.
unread.why: A single-patient HGPS case reports feasibility and short-term improvements in arterial stiffness, bone density, joint function, and inflammation after MSC infusions.

unread.title: Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement Combined With Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting in a Patient With Progeria.
unread.why: The case provides a concrete surgical option for symptomatic HGPS with severe aortic stenosis and coronary disease when less invasive approaches are unsuitable.

unread.title: Baricitinib Augments Lonafarnib Therapy to Preserve Colonic Homeostasis and Microbial Balance in a Mouse Model of Progeria.
unread.why: The study demonstrates that baricitinib combined with lonafarnib improves colonic architecture, inflammation, senescence, fibrosis, and microbial balance in progeria mice.

unread.title: Lonafarnib clinical trials demonstrate uncoupling of the muscle-bone unit in Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome.
unread.why: The study establishes pQCT muscle-bone measurements as clinical outcome measures and benchmarks their longitudinal changes in HGPS patients receiving lonafarnib.

unread.title: Lamins A and C but not lamin B1 regulate nuclear mechanics.
unread.why: The study provides cellular models and quantitative assays for nuclear mechanics directly relevant to the lamin A/C biology of Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome.

unread.title: Rapamycin reverses cellular phenotypes and enhances mutant protein clearance in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome cells.
unread.why: Rapamycin directly reverses nuclear blebbing and senescence and enhances progerin clearance in HGPS fibroblasts, providing a tested drug and cellular model.

unread.title: Progressive vascular smooth muscle cell defects in a mouse model of Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome.
unread.why: The engineered mouse reproduces progressive vascular smooth-muscle-cell loss and is explicitly positioned for testing HGPS therapies and cardiovascular disease mechanisms.

unread.title: Blocking protein farnesyltransferase improves nuclear shape in fibroblasts from humans with progeroid syndromes.
unread.why: FTI treatment experimentally reduces prelamin A nuclear-envelope accumulation and improves nuclear morphology in HGPS and other progeroid-syndrome fibroblasts.

unread.title: A farnesyltransferase inhibitor improves disease phenotypes in mice with a Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome mutation.
unread.why: An FTI improves growth, adipose mass, bone mineralization, rib fractures, and related phenotypes in a genetically engineered HGPS mouse model.

unread.title: A genome-wide CRISPR-based screen identifies KAT7 as a driver of cellular senescence.
unread.why: A genome-wide CRISPR screen in HGPS-derived mesenchymal cells identifies KAT7 inhibition as a senescence-reversing intervention that also improves progeroid mouse aging phenotypes.

unread.title: Increased progerin expression associated with unusual LMNA mutations causes severe progeroid syndromes.
unread.why: Patient fibroblasts with unusually progerin-rich HGPS phenotypes showed fewer misshapen nuclei after farnesyltransferase inhibition, demonstrating transferability of an established drug approach.
